section: Preparedness and response - surveillance, Epidemic Diseases Act, National Health Emergency framework
subsections: International Health Regulations 2005 - PHEIC, India's obligations

accepted.s: Under PM-ABHIM, what is the prescribed scale of Integrated Public Health Laboratories (IPHLs)?
accepted.x: PM-ABHIM provides for 744 Integrated Public Health Laboratories, with one IPHL in every district.
accepted.tq: Directly recall the programme component and its numerical scale.

accepted.s:
With reference to the Critical Care Hospital Blocks under PM-ABHIM, consider the following statements:
1. Their prescribed number is 631.
2. They are to be established in districts having more than five lakh people.
3. They are the same as Block Public Health Units established in 11 high-focus states.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: There are 631 Critical Care Hospital Blocks, intended for districts with more than five lakh people. Statement 3 is false because Block Public Health Units are a separate component with a scale of 3,389 in 11 high-focus states.
accepted.tq: Separate closely related programme components before selecting the coded combination.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the scale of Block Public Health Units under PM-ABHIM?
o: 631 units in districts with over five lakh people
accepted.x: PM-ABHIM provides 3,389 Block Public Health Units in 11 high-focus states.
accepted.tq: Match the exact institutional component with its number and coverage area.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs regarding Rural and Urban Health and Wellness Centres under PM-ABHIM is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The prescribed scale is 23,224 Rural Health and Wellness Centres and 13,736 Urban Health and Wellness Centres.
accepted.tq: Use the comparison row and watch for reversal of rural and urban figures.

accepted.s: Under the PM-ABHIM component relating to points of entry, preparedness is specified at:
accepted.x: Preparedness at 50 points of entry is included among the PM-ABHIM scales.
accepted.tq: Recall the small but distinct numerical figure rather than the larger programme totals.

accepted.s: In Andhra Pradesh, which combination correctly describes the PM-ABHIM facilities opened at Vijayawada?
o: 12 Critical Care Blocks and 10 IPHLs at a cost of Rs 744 crore
10 Critical Care Blocks and 12 Block Public Health Units at a cost of Rs 631 crore
10 Critical Care Blocks and 12 IPHLs at a cost of Rs 250 crore
12 Critical Care Blocks and 10 IPHLs at a cost of Rs 250 crore
accepted.x: At Vijayawada, 10 Critical Care Blocks and 12 Integrated Public Health Laboratories were opened at a cost of Rs 250 crore.
accepted.tq: Combine the location, facility numbers and expenditure figure without reversing paired numbers.

accepted.s: The International Health Regulations (2005) are best described as:
o: A domestic law enacted under the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897
A voluntary agreement administered by the World Bank
A legally binding instrument of the World Health Organization
A non-binding declaration adopted by BRICS
accepted.x: The IHR (2005) are a legally binding instrument of the World Health Organization.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a legally binding international health instrument from voluntary declarations and domestic laws.
accepted.sec: International Health Regulations 2005 - PHEIC, India's obligations

accepted.s: The International Health Regulations (2005) came into force in:
accepted.x: Although adopted as the IHR (2005), the Regulations came into force in 2007.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year in the title from the year of entry into force.
accepted.sec: International Health Regulations 2005 - PHEIC, India's obligations

accepted.s:
Under the IHR (2005), Member States are required to:
1. Build core capacities for surveillance and response.
2. Report possible Public Health Emergencies of International Concern to WHO within 24 hours.
3. Designate a National IHR Focal Point.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three are obligations under the IHR (2005): building surveillance and response capacities, reporting possible PHEICs to WHO within 24 hours, and naming a National IHR Focal Point.
accepted.tq: Select the comprehensive option when all listed international obligations are supported.
accepted.sec: International Health Regulations 2005 - PHEIC, India's obligations

accepted.s: A country detects an event that may constitute a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. Under the IHR (2005), the possible PHEIC should be reported to WHO within:
accepted.x: The IHR (2005) require Member States to report possible PHEICs to WHO within 24 hours.
accepted.tq: Apply the reporting deadline to an operational surveillance scenario.
accepted.sec: International Health Regulations 2005 - PHEIC, India's obligations

accepted.s: Which of the following was added by the 2024 amendments to the IHR (2005)?
o: A higher tier called a pandemic emergency
A requirement to establish PM-ABHIM in every district
A replacement of WHO by the World Bank as the reporting authority
accepted.x: The 2024 amendments added a higher emergency tier termed a pandemic emergency. They did not abolish the PHEIC category or replace WHO as the relevant international health body.
accepted.tq: Identify the newly added tier while rejecting institutional and legal substitutions.
accepted.sec: International Health Regulations 2005 - PHEIC, India's obligations

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Ebola outbreak of May 2026:
1. It was declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern.
2. It met the criteria for the higher pandemic-emergency tier.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
accepted.x: The May 2026 Ebola outbreak was a PHEIC, but it did not meet the criteria for the higher pandemic-emergency tier.
accepted.tq: Separate the existing PHEIC category from the newly created higher pandemic-emergency tier.
accepted.sec: International Health Regulations 2005 - PHEIC, India's obligations

accepted.s: The WHO Pandemic Agreement was adopted on:
accepted.x: The WHO Pandemic Agreement was adopted on 20 May 2025.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the adoption date from dates associated with later reporting and outbreaks.
accepted.sec: International Health Regulations 2005 - PHEIC, India's obligations

accepted.s: Which of the following developments is associated with the BRICS New Delhi Declaration?
o: Adoption of the WHO Pandemic Agreement
Declaration of the May 2026 Ebola outbreak as a pandemic emergency
Creation of a sub-working group on an integrated early-warning system for infectious diseases
accepted.x: The BRICS New Delhi Declaration set up a sub-working group on an integrated early-warning system for infectious diseases.
accepted.tq: Match the international forum with its specific institutional outcome.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 is correct?
o: It was replaced by the 2017 draft Bill, which is already in force.
It has been criticised as colonial and for lacking a definition of dangerous epidemic disease and rights safeguards.
It applies only to non-infectious diseases.
It provides a detailed statutory definition of dangerous epidemic disease and comprehensive rights safeguards.
accepted.x: The 1897 Act is criticised as colonial and for lacking both a definition of dangerous epidemic disease and adequate rights safeguards.
accepted.tq: Find the option that accurately reflects the criticism rather than an exaggerated legal claim.

accepted.s:
With reference to the proposed legal framework for epidemic management, consider the following statements:
1. The 2017 draft Bill is still pending.
2. The 2017 draft Bill has already replaced the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
accepted.x: The 2017 draft Bill remains pending; it has not replaced the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897. Therefore, Statement 1 is correct and Statement 2 is false.
accepted.tq: Use the legal-status distinction between a pending draft and an enacted replacement.

accepted.s: Which of the following is associated with the Andhra Pradesh-specific preparedness and response measures?
o: Covid Pharma app and a zoonoses action plan in July 2026
The WHO Pandemic Agreement adopted in May 2025
A new pandemic-emergency tier under the IHR amendments
The BRICS New Delhi Declaration’s infectious-disease sub-working group
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh-specific measures include the Covid Pharma app and a zoonoses action plan launched in July 2026.
accepted.tq: Separate the State-specific initiatives from international legal and diplomatic developments.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the preparedness development mentioned for Andhra Pradesh in September 2026?
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh-specific current-affairs angle includes PM-ABHIM units opened in Vijayawada.
accepted.tq: Match the State location with the programme physically established there.

accepted.s: An advisory issued to States in May 2026 in the context of current infectious-disease preparedness was related to:
accepted.x: An Ebola advisory was issued to States in May 2026.
accepted.tq: Use the disease-specific cue to distinguish the advisory from other vector-borne diseases.
